scale.label: Strong
scale.desc: Shipped (GA), documented, and meets the criterion for FP&A use without custom development beyond normal configuration

scale.label: Partial
scale.desc: Exists but is limited in scope, generic (needs custom build to serve FP&A), or available only in preview or beta

scale.label: Gap
scale.desc: No native capability found. The customer must build it or buy another product. Announced-only features score Gap with an Announced tag

scale.label: Not documented
scale.desc: No public source found either way in this research. This is not the same as missing, and Vena should check its own Not documented cells first

scale.label: Descriptive
scale.desc: The report describes this row without a rating (who maintains it, architecture, published limits, pricing, maturity)

caveats.text: Omega is announced, not shipped. Every 2026 release frames cumulative context as future, BARC notes no specific timeline disclosed, and no pricing or SKU is public. Present Omega as roadmap direction and sell the GA agents, MCP and planning platform.

Running Omega on a customer's Databricks is not public. No public source confirms a customer-Databricks deployment, a Databricks partnership, Delta Sharing or Unity Catalog integration, and Vena AI is described as built on Azure and Azure OpenAI. Only Morpheo's pre-acquisition site lists Databricks and Snowflake, as source connectors. Do not claim it externally until Vena publishes it.

MCP write-back is contradictory. The Excelerate release and Spring '26 notes describe plan updates and write-back, but the developer docs list only read tools. Say read access documented, write-back announced until docs change.

Microsoft Fabric Planning competes directly. A Lumel-built, first-party EPM workload is GA as part of the Fabric SKU, metered from August 1, 2026, with zero-copy planning on Power BI semantic models, and it overlaps Acterys' Power BI write-back pitch. Prepare a Fabric Planning battlecard focused on consolidation, Excel and agentic planning.

Morpheo was early-stage at acquisition. It had 7 employees, launched Omega as preview only in November 2025, and listed security as SOC2 Initiated. Avoid enterprise-maturity claims for Omega until Vena publishes controls.

Some Vena capabilities are not publicly documented. Allocations and cell-level security did not appear in the Vena sources reviewed, the Scenario Agent is Coming Soon, and Operational Tables are Open Beta. Confirm internally before rating these Strong on a public page.

Competitor status changes monthly. Snowflake renamed Snowflake Intelligence to CoWork, Databricks renamed Genie spaces to Genie Agents, Google renamed Dataplex to Knowledge Catalog, and many cited features are preview. Re-verify statuses before each publish.

leads.text: Snowflake has no native planning product. Snowplan, its internal planning app for 40+ entities, needed a custom Streamlit interface, write-back, versioned scenarios, review and approval, and row-level controls.
Snowflake points customers to Forward Deployed Finance Specialists rather than a product, and its SVP of Finance concedes not every finance team has engineers inside the function.
Vena ships versions, approvals, consolidation, audit history and Excel write-back as product.
Vena's Planning Agent writes plans inside governed workflows, while Snowflake agents write only through procedures a developer builds.
Snowflake's Multi-Party Approval is a governance four-eyes control, not a budget submission workflow.
Snowflake's Excel Extension is GA soon with no write-back shown, while Vena is native Excel.

lags.text: Snowflake's learning loop is real and shipping. Verified-query suggestions and Autopilot propose updates that humans certify, and Vena has nothing equivalent documented.
Snowflake ships per-user CoWork memory while Omega is announced.
Snowflake leads on agent orchestration and MCP breadth.
Snowflake wins on data gravity, with zero-copy SAP and Salesforce GA and Workday in private preview.
Parity on semantic layer and natural language query. Vena is finance-specific, Snowflake broader. Neither side has independent accuracy figures.

talkTrack: Snowflake is an excellent place to keep and query finance data, and its AI on top of that data is moving fast.
What Snowflake does not sell is a planning application. Its own finance team had to build one on Streamlit, and Snowflake sends customers forward-deployed specialists to do the same.
Vena gives you versions, approvals, consolidation, audit and Excel write-back from day one, plus GA agents that update plans inside that workflow.

leads.text: Genie is explicitly read-only, and Excel write-back supports table-level writes only, with no row-level updates, appends or merges.
Databricks positions itself as the foundation under finance, and its planning accelerator pairs the lakehouse and Genie with BOARD for plan versions and scenarios.
Established planning vendors connect to Databricks one way. Pigment is import-only with no write-back and Anaplan uses a read pipeline.
Vena's MCP Server is GA while Databricks' managed MCP servers are public preview.
Vena's Planning Agent writes plans today, while Genie is read-only and MCP writes are Beta.

lags.text: Genie Ontology is the most direct competitor to the context-accumulates-with-use story, framed as model the head and learn the tail.
Databricks publishes internal accuracy claims, such as 32% to over 90% on an internal benchmark, which no Vena figure matches, though none are independent.
Databricks leads on orchestration with the GA Supervisor Agent.
Databricks leads on data in place through OpenSharing.
Pilot economics favor Databricks. Genie usage by human users is free through January 31, 2027.
Its learning is still curated. Genie Ontology learns from analytics artifacts, not planning events, and agent behavior does not change on user feedback alone.

If you want plans, approvals and consolidation, you either build a CPM product on Lakebase or you buy one. Vena is the one your finance team can run without engineers.

leads.text: Allocations and financial consolidation do not appear in the Planning pages reviewed, and AI agents for mid-cycle course correction are a roadmap item.
Vena's consolidation shipped GA on August 26, 2026 and its Planning Agent went GA on May 13, 2026.

Planning write-back goes only to Fabric SQL and does not update the connected semantic model, each plan item is tied to one semantic model, users without an RLS role see union of all role data, and write-back caps at 1.2 million cells.
Data agents are capped at 25 rows by 25 columns per answer, cannot write, and are English only, which matters for bilingual Canadian finance teams.
Vena runs in native Excel, while Planning offers an Excel-like web grid with import and export and no documented Excel add-in.
Vena already works in Microsoft surfaces, with Vena Copilot for Teams GA since May 15, 2025 and the MCP Server supporting Microsoft Copilot as a client.

lags.text: Microsoft wins on procurement. Planning, Copilot and data agents draw on Fabric capacity a customer may already own, with reservations saving about 41% over pay-as-you-go.
Microsoft is at parity on core planning mechanics, with scenarios, what-if, write-back, multi-level approvals with change history, and Teams integration.
Microsoft leads on data access, with zero-copy planning on Power BI semantic models and OneLake shortcuts.
Fabric Planning overlaps Acterys directly, since Acterys pitches Power BI and Fabric write-back planning.
Microsoft's first-party planning partner is Lumel, not Vena. This research could not confirm whether Acterys or Vena ships as a native Fabric workload.
Governance through Purview DLP, audit and eDiscovery applies to data agents.

talkTrack: Fabric Planning is a solid budgeting grid on your Power BI models, and it bills on capacity you already own.

Before you standardize on it, ask three questions. Where does consolidation happen, with eliminations and FX? Will your team work in a web grid or in Excel? What does the AI actually do in the plan today?
Microsoft lists agentic planning as roadmap, while Vena's Planning Agent is GA.
Vena runs on the same Microsoft stack, in Excel, in Power BI through Acterys, and in Teams and Copilot through MCP.

leads.text: Vena's Planning Agent and MCP Server are GA today, while SAP's planning agents were scheduled for Q3 2026 and delivery could not be verified.
Vena's consolidation handles multi-ERP environments, which matters in mixed estates where SAP's context is strongest on SAP data.
SAP's commercial terms carry lock-in signals. BDC must be sold with at least one Intelligent Application, and seamless planning requires the same data center and one-to-one tenants.
SAP's MCP support is announced for Joule Studio, while Vena's MCP Server is GA.

lags.text: SAP ships a native planning engine, a business context graph and finance agents under one Capacity Unit contract.
SAP documents allocations and value driver trees where Vena's public sources do not show allocations.
SAP leads on zero-copy data, with BDC Connect to all four major data platforms.
Parity on planning application and Excel write-back.
A third party reports bidirectional Delta Sharing with Databricks GA since September 2025.

build: If SAP-centric, relatively little
Configure SAC models, data actions and driver trees
Integrate non-SAP data through BDC Connect or Datasphere
Adopt the Joule planning agents as they ship
SAC calendar workflows, audit logs, data access control and the consolidation path were not verified
talkTrack: If you run on SAP, SAC is a credible planning tool, and SAP is wrapping it in a strong data and context story.
Ask what is shipped versus scheduled. Vena's Planning Agent and MCP server are GA today, and SAP's planning agents and MCP support are on the roadmap.
If your entities run on more than one ERP, Vena consolidates across them without tying planning to one vendor's data cloud.

providers.name: Palantir (Foundry Ontology and AIP)
providers.headline: vs Palantir Foundry Ontology and AIP
providers.summary: Palantir's Ontology is both the semantic layer and a transactional, audited write-back layer, and Ontology MCP enables controlled writes by external agents, which makes it the closest architectural analogue to context plus orchestrated actions. It ships no packaged FP&A semantics, so every finance concept must be modeled by the customer.

leads.text: Palantir ships no packaged FP&A semantics. Versions, spreading, allocations, rollups, consolidation and an Excel front end would all have to be engineered on the Ontology.
Finance examples found are government-oriented, and no commercial FP&A planning reference on Foundry was found.
Vena ships native Excel, while Palantir's Excel interface is not documented.

lags.text: Palantir is the closest analogue to context layer plus orchestrated actions, with governed transactional write-back and audit documented today.
External-agent writes through Ontology MCP are documented, while Vena's MCP write-back is not in its docs.
Palantir leads on agent orchestration with AIP Logic and pro-code agents.
Parity on audit, with Palantir action logs against Vena audit history.

build: FP&A ontology (accounts, entities, versions, scenarios)
Planning calculations in functions or AIP Logic
Input grids and approval gates in Workshop and actions
Excel interface
Agent memory pattern
talkTrack: Palantir gives you a powerful, governed foundation, and it can absolutely power bespoke decision apps.
For FP&A, though, you would be designing the planning model, the calculations, the approvals and the Excel experience yourself.
Vena ships that as product, and the two can coexist.
Treat any claim that Omega could read the Palantir Ontology through Ontology MCP as an untested idea, not a Vena feature.

effortNote: No published, quantified estimate of team size, months or run cost for building FP&A planning on Snowflake, Databricks, Fabric or BigQuery was found, and sales should not quote effort numbers in either direction. Snowflake's Snowplan v2 is the best primary evidence but discloses no team size, budget or performance metrics, and proves feasibility rather than typical effort. The complexity column is the author's relative judgment, not a sourced figure. Vena's own implementation effort is also unpublished, so the fair comparison is configure a CPM product against build one.
openQuestions: What is Omega's release status today (private preview, beta, GA) and its dated roadmap, and do Acterys customers get it first, as one analyst reports? Every external page must otherwise label Omega Announced.

Can Omega run in or against a customer's Databricks, Fabric/OneLake or Snowflake, and does it use zero-copy access (Delta Sharing, OneLake shortcuts) or copy data into Vena? Vena's D3 and D4 cells and the Databricks talk track depend on it.
Which Morpheo capabilities ship inside Vena Omega, and when? Morpheo claimed 500+ connectors and Smart Contracts as coming soon, and connector breadth would lift Vena's D1 and D2 ratings.
Where is cumulative context stored, and how is it versioned, permissioned, audited, inspected and corrected? BARC's main risk is whether outputs stay explainable and permission-aware.
Is MCP write-back shipped, and do AI-initiated writes route through workflow approvals? Marketing says write-back while docs list read tools only.
Are allocations and cell-level security supported, and where are they documented? Both are Not documented in Vena's public sources, while SAP documents allocations.
What are Omega's pricing and packaging (seats, platform or consumption), and how do they compare with Fabric capacity meters?

Does Vena AI support French and other languages for natural language queries, and in which Azure regions is it processed? Fabric data agents are English only, so a documented answer could be a Vena differentiator in Canada.
Will Vena or Acterys ship as a native Fabric workload via the Extensibility Toolkit, and how does Acterys position against Fabric Planning? Microsoft's first-party planning partner is Lumel.
Should Vena join OSI / Apache Ossie? No planning vendor is a member.
What security attestation covers Omega, given Morpheo listed SOC2 Initiated?
Is there customer proof with measured outcomes for Omega, and can the industry's only cumulative context engine claim be substantiated? Snowflake and Databricks both market learning context layers.
